rawFindings.claim: Modified Phase 0.5 exit gate requires Host-supervised agent-replacement semantics that are defined nowhere in the authoritative executable spec (§0.5 scope, deliverables, and tests were not updated to match)
rawFindings.description: The PR edits docs/phase-0-spec.md's Phase 0.5 exit gate to require that "Agent replacement/restart does not invalidate Host-owned execution identity or durable state — the Host supervises the Agent, so replacing or restarting the Agent process preserves operation identity, session state, and canonical events." However, the authoritative §0.5 that this gate belongs to (unchanged by the PR) is titled "Durable cognition integration" and specifies only an in-process `extensions/cognition` adapter plus `packages/cognition-runtime/{coordinator,policy,reinforcement,consolidation}` package, with crash/concurrency tests that assume a single process (kill process mid-task → reopen → replay). There is no Host control plane, no Agent Supervisor, no Agent Protocol, no separate Agent process, and no agent-replacement test anywhere in the spec's §0.5 scope, deliverables, or required tests. Repo-wide search confirms "Agent Protocol" appears only in the new docs/roadmap.md, and the only "host" concept in the spec is `StaticExtensionHost` — an in-process extension mount seam in packages/agent-core, not a supervising runtime. This creates a normative contract violation under the repo's own rules: docs/rules.md and docs/constitution.md declare phase gates executable and authoritative, and roadmap.md itself states that "the executable specification with authoritative gate definitions lives in phase-0-spec.md." The gate now demands a proof that the specified single-process architecture cannot produce: as specified, killing the process kills loop and coordinator together, and recovery is via event replay — there is no replaceable Agent whose replacement must preserve Host state. When Phase 0.5 is implemented, the exit gate is either unsatisfiable as specified or silently diverges from the roadmap's Host/Agent architecture (which also places the Agent Protocol and transactional scheduler 'here'). Fix by either adding the Host control plane / Agent Protocol / agent-replacement test scope to §0.5, or rewording the exit-gate clause to match the spec's actual architecture.

proof.summary: Static trace: the changed exit-gate text (spec lines 541-551) references 'the Host supervises the Agent' / agent-replacement guarantees; the enclosing unchanged §0.5 (spec lines 490-540) defines only extensions/cognition + packages/cognition-runtime with single-process crash tests; 'Agent Protocol' matches only docs/roadmap.md; the only 'host' in the spec is StaticExtensionHost (in-process, packages/agent-core). Under rules.md's executable-gate contract and roadmap.md's own 'authoritative gate definitions live in phase-0-spec.md' declaration, the gate references undefined, unscoped machinery.

rawFindings.claim: findCommentByMarker JSDoc still documents the ambiguous result as { ambiguous: true, comments: [] } while the implementation returns the populated matches array
rawFindings.description: The PR rewrote the pagination doc block but left the @returns line claiming 'Returns { ambiguous: true, comments: [] } if multiple matches found.' Both return paths (the in-loop early exit and the post-loop fallback) return { ambiguous: true, comments: matches } with exactly the 2+ matched comments. The populated array is load-bearing: postMarkedComment builds detail.matchCount from existing.comments.length, and triageWorker includes result.detail?.matchCount in its blocking error message. The doc contradicts the executable contract of the function it annotates and should be corrected to 'comments: <matched comments>'.

proof.summary: Full read of commentMarkers.js at HEAD shows the @returns claim (comments: []) at lines 53-54 while lines 81-84 and the final return path produce { ambiguous: true, comments: matches }; postMarkedComment (same file) reads existing.comments.length for matchCount.

rawFindings.claim: Full pagination converts historically duplicated markers (spread past page 1, created by the pre-fix bug this PR corrects) into permanently failing triage jobs
rawFindings.description: Before this change, findCommentByMarker searched only page 1; when pre-existing duplicate marker comments both lived on page 2+ the old code returned null and posted yet another duplicate (spammy, but triage succeeded). Now the full scan proves ambiguity, postMarkedComment returns action 'blocked', and triageIssue throws, which abandons the idempotency lease and sends the job to BullMQ retry. Ambiguity is a persistent state, so classifyTriageFailure will keep classifying the generic Error as retryable and every retry will throw again until attempts are exhausted — those issues will never complete triage (no updated summary/labels) until an operator manually deletes the duplicate comments. This matches the PR's stated design ('operator can clean up the duplicates'), but it is a behavior regression for issues poisoned by the exact bug being fixed: previously-succeeding re-triage becomes a hard failure. Consider a distinct failure class or alert for marker_ambiguous instead of generic retry, and/or documenting the cleanup runbook for deployments upgrading past this change.

proof.summary: Static trace of the full triageWorker.js at HEAD: the gated block (lines 346-355) now runs postMarkedComment for every triaged issue; postMarkedComment returns {action:'blocked', reason:'marker_ambiguous'} when findCommentByMarker reports ambiguity (newly reachable for page-2+ duplicates via the early exit at commentMarkers.js lines 80-84), and triageIssue throws on result.action === 'blocked', which propagates through the outer catch, abandons the lease, and rethrows for BullMQ retry.

The normative contract for pillars.triage.auto_comment could not be located. This PR changes the flag's effective meaning from 'post a comment only for needs_more_info/duplicate_hint' to 'post exactly one summary comment on every successfully triaged issue (default on)'. If the .gitwire.yml schema/docs, @gitwire/rules package, or config validation describe auto_comment with the narrower meaning, this is a config-contract violation and a large behavioral change for every existing deployment with auto_comment unset; if the docs describe the broader meaning (as the PR and its tests claim), the change is the intended fix. Searches for 'auto_comment' at both SHAs returned empty results, so the documented contract is unverified.

Other pre-existing test suites that exercise triageIssue's comment behavior could not be inspected.
